## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible walk1 (math+decide→mask) with a simple host-scan walk2 can approach the streaming ceiling, with respawn overhead scaling in death rate.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p falls from 10.888 (N=4000) to 6.631 (N=16000) — overhead amortization below N=16000, since the L1d spill at N≈949 is already passed at the smallest measured point. From N=16000 through N=4000000 the curve is flat (6.583–6.88 ns/p), showing no knee at the L2→DRAM spill (N≈60787). Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: at q=0.25 the plateau sits at 8.42–8.89 ns/p versus 6.58–6.88 at q=0.01, a uniform ~2 ns/p shift preserving the flat N-shape.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 10.48 GB/s at N=65000, q=0.01 — 41.6% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. The cell is overhead-bound below N=16000 (6.34 GB/s at N=4000), then settles to ~10.4 GB/s with no ceiling approach. Death rate erodes the large-N regime gradually: at q=0.05, N=4000000 drops to 8.83 GB/s; at q=0.25 the plateau is 7.77–8.19 GB/s (31–33% of ceiling). The overhead→steady transition occurs by N=16000; the steady→death-rate-limited transition is gradual, driven by the 34 `bl` respawn calls rising with churn.

## Assembly
No vectorization of particle math — all float ops use scalar `s` registers (`ldp s5, s6`, `fadd s5, s5, s3`, `fmul s5, s5, s4`, `fsub s5, s3, s6`, `fcvtzs w15, s5`). The histogram reports 0 vector-suffixed instructions, though the excerpt shows NEON confined to the mask-scan OR-reduction (`ldp q1, q0`, `orr.16b v0, v1, v0`, `ext.16b v1, v0, v0, #0x8`, `orr.8b v0, v0, v1`). No gather exists. The pixel scatter is byte-granular: `ldrb w2, [x1]`, `add w2, w2, w12`, `csel w2, w2, w11, lo`, `strb w2, [x1]` — three dependent load-modify-store chains per pixel with `csel` clamping. The 34 `cbz` and 34 `bl` to `_layouts.L1.data.Data.spawn` reflect the unrolled per-byte respawn scan. Scalar math plus byte-granular scatter explains the 42% ceiling cap.

## Verdict
Refuted — the cell never exceeds 10.48 GB/s (42% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at any N or death rate. The Halide-expressible walk1 compiles to scalar `s`-register math with no particle vectorization, and the byte-granular scatter (`ldrb`/`csel`/`strb`) cannot stream. Death rate raises the floor from 6.58 to 8.42 ns/p (q=0.01→0.25) without changing the N-shape, confirming the bottleneck is code structure, not memory hierarchy.
